finalText:
Migration finished. `verify.js` passes: `OK every db.query call site moved to db.execute, and nothing else moved`.

**What changed** — 36 call sites across 12 files, all rewritten from `db.query(sql, params)` to `db.execute({ sql, params })`:

| Package | Files |
|---|---|
| accounts | `repo/session.js`, `admin/apiKeyAdmin.js`, `service/teamService.js` |
| analytics | `repo/cohort.js` |
| billing | `repo/refund.js`, `service/couponService.js` |
| catalog | `repo/supplier.js`, `admin/variantAdmin.js` |
| orders | `repo/shipment.js`, `service/returnService.js` |
| support | `repo/sla.js`, `admin/macroAdmin.js` |

**What I deliberately left alone:**

- **`vendor/legacy-orm/adapter.js`** — two `db.query` calls remain. The file's header says it's a vendored copy of legacy-orm 2.1.4, replaced wholesale on upgrade, so local edits would be silently lost. Worth flagging: those two sites will break when the driver's next major drops `query`, so the real fix is upstreaming the change or pinning/wrapping the adapter — but that's a separate decision, not part of this sweep.
- **`cache.query(...)`** — 25 call sites across the repo. Different object, unrelated API; the name collision is coincidental.

A note on method: the args weren't uniformly simple — the `update*` functions pass `[...keys.map((k) => patch[k]), id]`, which contains a comma inside a nested call. I used a balanced-paren/string-aware walker to split arguments rather than a comma regex, which would have split that array in the wrong place and produced a malformed `params:`. The codemod was run from a scratch file outside the repo and deleted afterward, so no stray module landed in `packages/` (the verifier asserts a 75-module count).
